2608.22077.title: Spine-Branch Coordination for Multi-agent Computer Use
2608.22077.paper_summary: Computer use agents (CUAs) are increasingly deployed as multi-agent systems that decompose a task into multiple subtasks executed across parallel virtual machines (VMs). However, a critical physical bottleneck is that the state of two VMs cannot be merged. Previous systems handle this ad-hoc rather than treating it as a first-class concern. We propose Spine-Branch Coordination for multi-agent computer use, a framework that decomposes a task into a "spine-branch" graph, where the spine carries the main task flow with continuous VM state and branch tasks execute in parallel to collect information the spine needs to complete the task. Branch VMs are discarded once their tasks finish, so no VM merging ever occurs. Experiments show that on 200 long-horizon tasks from Odysseys and across three CUA backbones, Spine-Branch improves success rate over the baseline system by 6.0% to 16.5%, while reducing per-task cost by 34% to 70%, indicating that explicitly modeling VM-state merging constraint enables multi-agent computer use to scale efficiently.
2608.22077.paper_summary_zh: 電腦使用代理（CUAs）越來越多地被部署為多代理系統，將任務分解為多個子任務，並在平行虛擬機（VMs）上執行。<lb/>然而，一個關鍵的物理瓶頸是兩個虛擬機的狀態無法合併。<lb/>以往的系統以臨時方式處理這一問題，而不是將其視為一個首要關注點。<lb/>我們提出了脊樹分支協調（Spine-Branch Coordination）用於多代理電腦使用，這是一個將任務分解為「脊樹-分支」圖的框架，其中脊樹承載著主要的任務流程，並且持續的虛擬機狀態，而分支任務則並行執行以收集脊樹完成任務所需的信息。<lb/>一旦分支虛擬機的任務完成，它們將被丟棄，因此不會發生虛擬機合併。<lb/>實驗顯示，在來自Odysseys的200個長期任務和三個CUA骨幹上，脊樹分支相較於基線系統提高了6.0%至16.5%的成功率，同時每個任務的成本降低了34%至70%，這表明明確建模虛擬機狀態合併約束使多代理電腦使用能夠高效擴展。
